title: Datong Walks: Expo Park, Lin An Tai and Dalongdong Temples
excerpt: Two self-guided walks from Yuanshan MRT: an East route of about 3km through the weekend Expo Farmer's Market, the Fine Arts Museum, Xinsheng Park and Lin An Tai, and a West route of about 1.5km to the Baoan and Confucius temples and Dalong Street Night Market.
content:
Both of these walks set out from Yuanshan MRT, on the northern edge of Datong, and go in opposite directions. The East route crosses Taipei Expo Park and Xinsheng Park, calling at the weekend farmer's market, the Fine Arts Museum, Lin An Tai and the indoor Collective Botanical Garden. It covers about 3km and takes about 5 to 6 hours with stops. The West route is a short loop to the Baoan and Confucius temples and Dalong Street Night Market, about 1.5km and about 3 to 4 hours.

This walk is best enjoyed at the weekend, when the big Expo Farmer's Market is running at Taipei Expo Park. Apart from the busy farmer's market, the temples, parks and other attractions are never very busy, even on weekends.

You could spend more time at the market, and only choose either the East or West route. The West route, with its temples and the Dalong Street Night Market, is the one to take in the evening. Taking both routes in one day needs roughly 8 to 10 hours.

The Routes

For somewhere to stay a few stops down the red line, see the Zhongshan hotel guide.

East Route: Expo Park, Museums and Xinsheng Park

  • 1 Arrive at Yuanshan MRT on the red Tamsui-Xinyi line after 10:00 and leave by exit 1
  • 2 Expo Farmer's Market is directly to the left
    • It runs every Saturday and Sunday from 10:00 to 18:00 on the roofed plaza at the Yumen Street entrance to the park
    • The city sets it up with farmers' associations from around Taiwan, so expect seasonal fruit and vegetables plus honey, jams, sauces and rice wine to take home
    • There is no market on weekdays
  • [optional] MAJI Square, a couple of minutes south-east of the market, is a cluster of restaurants and bars in shipping containers and wooden huts
    • It opens daily from 11:00 to 21:00, and some of the bars carry on well past midnight at weekends
    • The craft shops have gone: after the pandemic the operator dropped retail and turned the whole site over to food and drink
  • I would advise getting food here before taking the east route, as there aren't many options after this
  • Head east through the park and over Zhongshan North Road
  • 3 Turn north to the Taipei Story House
    • The mock-Tudor villa next to the museum was finished in 1914 for a wealthy tea merchant
    • Since 2021 the ACME group has run it as Maison ACME (圓山別邸), with small changing exhibitions inside and Cafe ACME beside it
    • Entry is free. Recent listings give 11:00 to 17:00 and closed on Mondays, but the hours vary between sources, so check before you go
  • 4 Visit the Taipei Fine Arts Museum next door
    • Opened in 1983, this was Taiwan's first museum given over to modern art
    • Open Tuesday to Sunday from 09:30 to 17:30, staying open until 20:30 on Saturdays, and closed on Mondays
    • A ticket costs NT$30, and on Saturday evenings entry is free from 17:00
  • 5 Head south through the park to where the Indigenous Cultural Centre stood
    • When this walk was first written, the centre sold indigenous craftwork, had a nice cafe inside and hosted aboriginal performances outside
    • It closed on 30 April 2022, and the building was pulled down in 2023 to clear the ground for the Fine Arts Museum's extension, most of which is going underground beneath this part of the park
    • Expect hoardings around the works until the extension opens, which reports have put at 2027 or 2028, and follow whichever paths are open
  • Head east through the floral tunnel and cross the main road, Xinsheng North Road
  • Enter Xinsheng Park and walk through the Rose Garden
    • It is free, never closes, and has more than 800 varieties of rose
    • The beds peak in March and April, during the Taipei Rose Festival (in 2026 it ended on 6 April); at other times of year expect far fewer flowers
  • Look out for the huge Grand Hotel to the north-west
  • 6 Head north-east to the Lin An Tai Ancestral House
    • An 18th-century Fujian-style family home that was taken apart on its original site in Da'an and put back together here
    • Free, and open Tuesday to Sunday. Doors open at 09:00 and close at 17:00 (last entry 16:45), or 18:00 in July and August
    • Closed on Mondays, over Lunar New Year, and on Tomb Sweeping Day and the Dragon Boat and Mid-Autumn festivals
  • 7 Re-enter the park and visit the Taipei Collective Botanical Garden
    • Its home is the glass Pavilion of Future from the 2010 Flora Expo, now a greenhouse with tropical, temperate, desert and alpine sections
    • Entry is free; it opens 09:00 to 17:00, Tuesday to Sunday
    • It is shut on Mondays, and if a public holiday lands on its closing day, the closure moves to the following day
  • 8 Head south-west through the garden to the maze
    • The Garden Maze is a free hedge maze at the southern end of Xinsheng Park, and a good place to let children run about

From the maze, either walk back towards the Expo to see the temples on the West route, or head home. Zhongshan Elementary School MRT, on the orange line, is about ten minutes south along Xinsheng North Road. Alternatively, take a bike from this YouBike station. The YouBike guide explains how to register and rent one.

West Route: Dalongdong Temples and Night Market

Best taken during the evening, after about 18:00. Both temples close at 21:00, and the Confucius Temple is shut all day on Mondays.

  • 1 From Yuanshan MRT, leave by exit 2, cross the road and head west along Kulun Street
  • Turn right into Dalong Street when you see signs for the temples
  • 2 Stop at the Baoan Temple Garden, a small garden with a pond across the road from the temple
  • 3 Visit Dalongdong Baoan Temple
    • Migrants from Tong'an in Fujian founded it in the 18th century for the Baosheng Emperor, a doctor who was later worshipped as a god of healing
    • Free, and open every day of the week from 06:00 to 21:00, Mondays included
  • 4 Cross Dalong Street to the Confucius Temple
    • Free, and open Tuesday to Sunday from 08:30 to 21:00, including public holidays; closed on Mondays
    • Free guided tours leave from the visitor centre at 10:30, 14:30 and 15:30, and groups of ten or more can book one in English a week ahead
    • Minglun Hall has a 94-seat theatre that plays two films, one a fantasy for children and the other a tour of the Dacheng Hall's architecture; screening times aren't published online, so ask at the visitor centre
    • The tours and films are daytime activities, so come before dark if you want them
  • 5 Head south to the Dalong Street Night Market where there are many local food options
    • The stalls fill the stretch of Dalong Street south of Jiuquan Street, from 16:00 until about 23:20, and until midnight on Saturdays and Sundays
    • In the mornings the same street sells breakfast instead, such as soy milk, egg wraps and porridge
  • 6 Turn left into Lane 208 of Chengde Road Section 3 and follow it east, across Chengde Road, back to Yuanshan MRT Station

Where to Eat

  • The Expo Farmer's Market has stalls selling snacks and drinks to eat as you walk round, alongside the produce
  • MAJI Square is the best place for a sit-down lunch before the East route, with international restaurants from late morning and bars in the evening
  • Cafe ACME, next to the Taipei Story House, is open daily from 10:00 to 18:00 and doesn't take bookings
  • After the museums there is almost nothing to eat until the end of the East route, so carry water and a snack through Xinsheng Park
  • Dalong Street Night Market is small and local, a few blocks of traditional stalls rather than a tourist market, and it suits a light dinner after the temples

Best Time to Go

Go on a Saturday or Sunday, as the farmer's market only runs at weekends. Take the East route in the morning, starting at about 10:00 when the market opens, because Lin An Tai and the Botanical Garden both close at 17:00. Take the West route in the evening: the night market starts at 16:00 and the temples stay open until 21:00, so after 18:00 you get both the temples and the stalls.

Saturday has the edge for doing both. The Fine Arts Museum stays open until 20:30 and is free from 17:00, which gives you a choice for the gap between the two routes.

Avoid Mondays. Lin An Tai, the Botanical Garden, the Story House, the Fine Arts Museum and the Confucius Temple are all closed, and there is no market. In spring the Rose Garden is at its best, and in July and August Lin An Tai stays open an hour later.

Getting There and Back

Start: Yuanshan station on the red Tamsui-Xinyi line. Use exit 1 for the East route, which comes out on the Expo Park side, and exit 2 for the West route, which is the exit the Baoan Temple recommends; the temple reckons on about 15 minutes' walk from there.

Finish: The East route ends at the maze in Xinsheng Park. Zhongshan Elementary School station on the orange line is about ten minutes' walk south, or you can walk back to Yuanshan. The West route is a loop and ends back at Yuanshan station. The MRT guide has fares and route details.

Common Questions

How long are the Datong walks?

The East route is about 3km from Yuanshan MRT to the maze in Xinsheng Park and takes about 5 to 6 hours with stops. The West route is a loop of about 1.5km and takes about 3 to 4 hours. Doing both takes most of a day.

Can I do both routes on the same day?

Yes, and a Saturday is the best day for it. Walk the East route from 10:00, rest at MAJI Square or the Fine Arts Museum in the late afternoon, then walk the West route after 18:00, when the night market is busy and the temples are still open.

Is the Indigenous Cultural Centre still open?

No. It closed in April 2022 and was demolished in 2023 to make room for the Fine Arts Museum's extension. The East route still passes the site on the way to the floral tunnel, but there are no longer performances or craft stalls here.

What is closed on Mondays?

Most of the East route: Lin An Tai, the Botanical Garden, the Story House and the Fine Arts Museum. The Confucius Temple is closed too. The Baoan Temple, the Rose Garden, MAJI Square and Dalong Street Night Market open every day, but the farmer's market only runs at weekends.

Do any of the stops charge for entry?

Only the Fine Arts Museum, which costs NT$30, and that is free on Saturday evenings from 17:00. The temples, Lin An Tai, the Story House, the Botanical Garden, the Rose Garden and the maze are all free.

Carry On Walking

Dadaocheng, Datong's old riverside trading quarter, is a few MRT stops south of Yuanshan; our Dadaocheng and Dihua Street walk covers it from the North Gate to Ningxia Night Market.
